page_positioning.subtitle: Cibinetide · 11-amino-acid EPO-derived peptide · pEQLERALNSS
page_positioning.hero_copy: ARA-290, also known as cibinetide, is an 11-amino-acid peptide built from the helix B surface of erythropoietin (EPO). Veracue supplies it as a research material for laboratory work. Unlike many research peptides, ARA-290 has real human evidence behind it -- it has been studied in Phase 2 clinical trials in sarcoidosis-associated neuropathy and type 2 diabetes, though those findings are specific to those patient populations. It is not FDA-approved, not intact EPO, and this material establishes no treatment effect or safety in people generally.

research_snapshot.value: ARA290, ARA 290, pHBSP, PHBSP, Pyroglutamate Helix B Surface Peptide
Modeled on the helix B surface domain of erythropoietin (EPO)
Investigated in multiple Phase 2 human studies (sarcoidosis-associated small-fiber neuropathy; type 2 diabetes with painful neuropathy)

what_is_ara_290.heading: What Is ARA-290?
body: ARA-290 is a synthetic 11-amino-acid peptide with the sequence pEQLERALNSS, built around the helix B surface region of erythropoietin (EPO). Cibinetide is the International Nonproprietary Name associated with the same molecule (CAS 1208243-50-8, PubChem CID 91810664) -- ARA-290 was its development code name, and both terms describe one compound.

It was designed by Araim Pharmaceuticals to investigate whether the tissue-protective signaling associated with EPO could be studied separately from EPO's classical erythropoietic activity -- the signaling that stimulates red blood cell production. That research question, not a marketed product, is why ARA-290 exists as a distinct compound in the literature rather than simply being studied as EPO.

ARA-290 is not erythropoietin. It is not recombinant EPO, and it is not a growth-hormone peptide. It is a short peptide fragment built around one surface region of a much larger 165-amino-acid glycoprotein hormone, and the literature treats it as pharmacologically distinct from EPO.

why_researchers_study.heading: Why Researchers Study ARA-290
why_researchers_study.body: ARA-290 occupies an unusual position among research peptides because of its structure-function research history: a defined design rationale (a fragment built from one surface of a known protein), an active area of receptor-biology debate, and an actual human clinical research record. Interest in the literature centers on a specific structural and translational research question -- whether EPO's tissue-protective signaling can be studied apart from its erythropoietic signaling -- which is why ARA-290 shows up in neurobiology, small-fiber research, tissue-protection signaling, and analytical peptide-characterization work rather than in hematology.

mechanism.heading: ARA-290 Mechanism and the Proposed Innate Repair Receptor
body: Erythropoietin's classical, erythropoietic effect is mediated through the EPO receptor homodimer (EPOR/EPOR) on erythroid precursor cells. Separately, EPO has also been reported to act on non-hematopoietic cells -- endothelial, neural, and cardiac tissue among others -- at higher concentrations than those needed for erythropoiesis, and researchers proposed that a different receptor complex might mediate these effects.

That proposed complex -- EPOR paired with the beta-common receptor (βcR/CD131) -- has been referred to in the literature as the innate repair receptor (IRR). ARA-290 was developed around this IRR model: a peptide built from the EPO helix B surface region, intended to engage IRR-linked signaling without engaging the EPOR homodimer responsible for erythropoiesis.

This receptor model is central to the ARA-290 literature, but it is not settled biology. A 2018 biophysical study (Cheung Tung Shing et al., Scientific Reports) tested the extracellular domains of EPOR and the beta-common receptor directly -- with and without EPO, and with and without ARA-290 -- using surface plasmon resonance, microscale thermophoresis, size-exclusion chromatography, pull-down assays, and analytical ultracentrifugation. Across all of these methods, the study found no detectable physical association between the two receptors' extracellular domains, and reported no requirement for the beta-common receptor in an in vivo mouse model of anemic stress recovery. The authors concluded that a direct extracellular EPOR-βc interaction was not supported by their data, while noting that transmembrane or intracellular regions of the receptors, not tested in that study, remain a possible site of interaction.

In short: IRR-linked signaling is a well-established research framework that has organized several decades of ARA-290 and cibinetide studies, including the human trials described below, but whether EPOR and the beta-common receptor physically associate at the molecular level remains an open, actively discussed question rather than confirmed receptor biology.
mechanism.language_note: This page uses 'proposed', 'has been reported', and 'research model' when describing IRR biology, rather than presenting it as an established receptor mechanism -- because the underlying molecular evidence is genuinely contested.

human_clinical_research.heading: Human Clinical Research
human_clinical_research.intro: ARA-290/cibinetide has an actual human clinical research history -- it has been investigated in randomized, controlled Phase 2 studies. The summary below describes specific published findings, not a claim that ARA-290 is an established or approved treatment for any condition.

evidence_table.population: Adults with biopsy-confirmed sarcoidosis and small-fiber neuropathy (n=22)
evidence_table.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study; intravenous ARA-290
evidence_table.endpoint_finding: Significant improvement on the Small Fiber Neuropathy Screening List (SFNSL) versus placebo, with improvement in some SF-36 quality-of-life dimensions
evidence_table.key_limitation: Small pilot cohort (n=22); pain-intensity improvement was similar between ARA-290 and placebo groups
evidence_table.citation: Heij L, et al. Safety and efficacy of ARA 290 in sarcoidosis patients with symptoms of small fiber neuropathy. Mol Med. 2012.

evidence_table.study_context: Sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and corneal nerve fiber density
evidence_table.population: Adults with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss
evidence_table.design: Randomized, controlled study measuring symptom scores and corneal confocal microscopy
evidence_table.endpoint_finding: Reported symptom improvement and increased corneal nerve fiber density versus comparator
evidence_table.key_limitation: Corneal nerve fiber density is a surrogate imaging endpoint, not a direct measure of clinical disease resolution
evidence_table.citation: ARA 290 improves symptoms in patients with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and increases corneal nerve fiber density. Mol Med. 2013.

evidence_table.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and painful neuropathy
evidence_table.design: Phase 2 study of daily subcutaneous ARA-290 versus placebo, evaluating metabolic and neuropathic endpoints
evidence_table.endpoint_finding: Reported improvements in metabolic control markers and neuropathic symptom measures during the study period
evidence_table.key_limitation: Diabetic-neuropathy population only; not generalizable to non-diabetic or healthy populations
evidence_table.citation: ARA 290, a nonerythropoietic peptide engineered from erythropoietin, improves metabolic control and neuropathic symptoms in patients with type 2 diabetes. Mol Med. 2014.

evidence_table.study_context: Corneal nerve fiber abundance, sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and neuropathic pain (Phase 2b)
evidence_table.population: Adults with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and neuropathic pain (n=64 across dose arms)
evidence_table.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2b trial of daily subcutaneous cibinetide (multiple dose arms) over 28 days
evidence_table.endpoint_finding: Dose-dependent increase in corneal nerve fiber area and regenerating intraepidermal nerve fibers at specific dose levels versus placebo
evidence_table.key_limitation: Findings were dose- and endpoint-specific, not uniform across all dose arms; imaging/biomarker endpoints, not a broad efficacy claim
evidence_table.citation: Cibinetide improves corneal nerve fiber abundance in patients with sarcoidosis-associated small nerve fiber loss and neuropathic pain. J Clin Med. 2018.

human_clinical_research.interpretation: Taken together, these studies establish that ARA-290/cibinetide has been investigated in controlled human trials and that specific endpoints changed in specific, indication-defined populations under specific dosing regimens. They do not establish that ARA-290 is an approved therapy, that it is safe or effective outside those studied populations and regimens, or that a Veracue research vial is equivalent to the investigational drug product used in these trials.

preclinical_research.heading: Preclinical Research
preclinical_research.intro: Preclinical (animal and in-vitro) findings are laboratory findings -- not evidence of a therapeutic effect in humans.

themes.note: Rodent models of peripheral nerve injury have examined functional and histological endpoints after ARA-290 administration.
Cell and organ-level studies have examined IRR-linked signaling in models of ischemic and inflammatory injury.
In-vitro work has explored anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic signaling proposed to run through IRR-linked pathways.
Studies in endothelial colony-forming cells and pancreatic islet models have examined proliferation, migration and resistance to stress-induced apoptosis.
Animal wound-healing and endothelial/vascular regeneration models have been reported in the preclinical literature.

preclinical_research.rule_note: No preclinical or animal finding on this page should be read as proof of a human therapeutic benefit.

what_evidence_does_not_establish.heading: What the ARA-290 Evidence Does Not Establish
bullets: That ARA-290 is an FDA-approved treatment for sarcoidosis, neuropathy, diabetes, or any other condition
That findings from sarcoidosis or type 2 diabetes clinical populations apply to healthy individuals
That preclinical/animal findings translate to a demonstrated human effect
That the innate repair receptor is settled receptor biology -- direct EPOR-βc association has been questioned by later biophysical work
That corneal nerve fiber density, neuropathy screening scores, or metabolic markers measured in these trials amount to a proven functional cure
That FDA or EMA orphan designation is the same as marketing authorization
That a Veracue RUO research vial is equivalent to the investigational drug product used in any cited clinical trial
That peptide-identity data (CAS, PubChem, UNII) alone establishes a specific lot's purity or quality

researcher_considerations.heading: Researcher Considerations When Evaluating ARA-290
researcher_considerations.intro: Practical information, analytical, procurement and evidence-interpretation points researchers actually run into with this compound.

items.problem: ARA-290 appears under several names across papers, databases and vendor listings.
items.solution: ARA-290, ARA290, ARA 290 and cibinetide all refer to the same molecule: sequence pEQLERALNSS, CAS 1208243-50-8, PubChem CID 91810664.

items.problem: ARA-290 can be confused with erythropoietin (EPO) itself, since it is described as 'EPO-derived.'
items.solution: ARA-290 is a short 11-amino-acid peptide built from one surface region of the much larger EPO protein. It is not intact EPO and not recombinant EPO.

items.problem: The pyroglutamate notation (pE, pGlu) at the N-terminus can be unfamiliar or ambiguous.
items.solution: pE denotes pyroglutamate, a cyclized glutamine residue at position 1 of the sequence. Reference sources sometimes write the sequence with an 'X' placeholder for this residue -- pEQLERALNSS and XEQLERALNSS describe the same molecule.

items.problem: Different peptide forms -- free peptide versus acetate or other salt forms -- produce different molecular-weight values.
items.solution: The 1257.3 g/mol figure on this page is the free-peptide molecular weight. Salt forms carry a different mass. Confirm which form a specific vial contains against that lot's own documentation rather than assuming.

items.problem: The 'innate repair receptor' is sometimes presented as an established, uncontested drug target.
items.solution: Treat IRR biology as a research model, not settled fact. It organizes much of the ARA-290 literature, but a 2018 biophysical study found no direct association between the EPOR and beta-common receptor extracellular domains -- see the Mechanism section above for the specific finding.

items.problem: Findings from animal or in-vitro tissue-protection models can be cited as if they were human results.
items.solution: Keep animal, in-vitro and human evidence in clearly separate categories. This page's evidence tables label each study's population and design for exactly that reason.

items.problem: Results from small Phase 2 clinical studies get generalized into broad efficacy claims online.
items.solution: Check the population (sarcoidosis, type 2 diabetes), the study design (pilot vs. Phase 2b, sample size), and the specific endpoint measured before repeating any human finding -- the Human Clinical Research table gives all three for each cited study.

items.problem: Searches for 'ARA-290 benefits' mostly surface promotional summaries rather than what was actually measured.
items.solution: Read a 'benefits' claim as a question about a specific measured endpoint -- which symptom score, imaging measure, or lab marker changed, in which population, under which regimen -- not as a general wellness outcome.

items.problem: Historical clinical-trial dosing protocols can be mistaken for instructions for using a research vial.
items.solution: Trial dosing described in the literature is study-design context only. It is not administration guidance for any Veracue material, which is not for human or animal use.

items.problem: Molecule identity and lot identity are not the same thing.
items.solution: PubChem/CAS/UNII data describe the reference molecule in general. A specific vial's identity and purity can only be confirmed by that lot's own analytical documentation -- sequence/mass-spec match, HPLC purity, and lot number together.

items.problem: A purity percentage on a COA doesn't by itself establish that a vial contains ARA-290.
items.solution: Purity and identity are separate questions. A useful COA states the analytical method, reports an observed mass or sequence-identity result, and ties both to a specific lot number and test date.

items.problem: Procurement teams need to know exactly what Veracue has and hasn't documented for this material.
items.solution: See the Product Specifications table below. Every field is either a first-party Veracue fact or is marked as not yet published -- nothing is filled in from a competitor listing or a generic reference value.

faq.question: What is ARA-290?
faq.answer: ARA-290 is a synthetic 11-amino-acid peptide (sequence pEQLERALNSS) built from the helix B surface region of erythropoietin (EPO), studied as a non-erythropoietic research compound.

faq.question: Is ARA-290 the same as cibinetide?
faq.answer: Yes. Cibinetide is the International Nonproprietary Name for the peptide historically developed and studied as ARA-290 -- they share the same CAS number (1208243-50-8) and PubChem record (CID 91810664).

faq.question: What is the ARA-290 sequence?
faq.answer: pEQLERALNSS -- an 11-residue sequence with an N-terminal pyroglutamate (pE), corresponding to pE-Glu-Gln-Leu-Glu-Arg-Ala-Leu-Asn-Ser-Ser.

faq.question: What is the molecular weight of ARA-290?
faq.answer: The free peptide has an average molecular weight of 1257.3 g/mol (molecular formula C51H84N16O21). Salt forms, such as an acetate, carry a different molecular weight -- confirm which form applies to a specific lot before using this figure in calculations.

faq.question: What is ARA-290 derived from?
faq.answer: It is built around the helix B surface domain of erythropoietin (EPO) -- a defined structural region of the much larger EPO protein -- rather than being EPO itself.

faq.question: How does ARA-290 relate to erythropoietin?
faq.answer: ARA-290 was designed to investigate whether the tissue-protective signaling associated with EPO could be studied separately from EPO's classical erythropoietic activity. It is not intact EPO and is not recombinant EPO.

faq.question: What is the proposed innate repair receptor?
faq.answer: A receptor complex proposed in the literature as the erythropoietin receptor (EPOR) paired with the beta-common receptor (βcR/CD131), hypothesized to mediate non-erythropoietic, tissue-protective signaling. Direct physical association between the two receptors' extracellular domains has not been confirmed and was specifically not detected in a 2018 biophysical study -- it remains an active area of scientific discussion rather than settled receptor biology.

faq.question: What human research has investigated ARA-290?
faq.answer: Randomized, controlled Phase 2 human studies have investigated ARA-290/cibinetide in sarcoidosis-associated small-fiber neuropathy and in type 2 diabetes with painful neuropathy, measuring endpoints such as neuropathy symptom scores, corneal nerve fiber density, and metabolic markers.

faq.question: What did the sarcoidosis studies report?
faq.answer: Published studies reported improved small-fiber neuropathy symptom scores and increased corneal nerve fiber density versus placebo or comparator in sarcoidosis patients with small nerve fiber loss -- findings specific to that population and study design, not a general treatment claim.

faq.question: What did the type 2 diabetes study report?
faq.answer: A Phase 2 study in adults with type 2 diabetes and painful neuropathy reported improvements in metabolic control markers and neuropathic symptom measures during the study period -- a finding specific to that population.

faq.question: Is ARA-290 FDA approved?
faq.answer: No. ARA-290/cibinetide is not an FDA-approved drug. FDA orphan drug designation for sarcoidosis was granted on June 13, 2016, and EU orphan designations followed in 2013 and 2016, but orphan designation is a development incentive, not a marketing authorization.

faq.question: What should an ARA-290 COA contain?
faq.answer: A useful Certificate of Analysis states the analytical method used, reports an observed identity/mass result rather than just the theoretical reference mass, and ties both to a specific lot number and test date -- see the COA guidance section above for a full checklist.
